title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page 31 of a typed draft headed 'CHAPITRE II (Etat 1) – FONCTIONS HOLOMORPHES D'UNE VARIABLE COMPLEXE, §1 Le principe du prolongement analytique'. The style (K = R or C, E a complete normed space, 'série entière sommable', polycylindres, 'Etat 1') is that of a Bourbaki working draft. Grothendieck evidently used such sheets as scratch paper, so it sits between his manuscript pages on Dedekind/Tannakian categories, Pordet, Ram, Eq(C,T) and Bord(C,T). Those neighbouring pages are probably on the other side of such sheets.

The content is the identity theorem for convergent power series in several variables. Let P and Q be open polycylinders in K^p with centres a and b and non-empty intersection. Let f be the sum of a power series in (x_i − a_i), summable on P, and g the sum of a power series in (x_i − b_i), summable on Q, both E-valued. If f = g on a non-empty open set U ⊂ P∩Q, then f = g on all of P∩Q.

The proof runs as follows:
- P∩Q is convex, so for x ∈ U and y ∈ P∩Q the segment [x, y] lies in P∩Q.
- h(t) = f(x + t(y−x)) − g(x + t(y−x)) is real-analytic on an open interval I ⊃ [0, 1].
- Let ρ = sup A, where A = {t ∈ [0, 1] : h(s) = 0 for 0 ≤ s ≤ t}. Then ρ > 0 because U is open, and ρ ∈ A by continuity.
- If ρ < 1, expand h as a power series in t − ρ. Since h vanishes on [0, ρ], the isolated zeros principle forces all coefficients to vanish, so h = 0 on (ρ, ρ+α) for some α > 0. This contradicts the definition of ρ; the conclusion is on the next typed page, which is not shown.

The result is standard connectedness/analytic continuation, presented as the first step toward analytic continuation of holomorphic functions.
errors: No mathematical error. The step that h is analytic at ρ uses the standard fact that a power series sum is analytic at every interior point of its domain of convergence; the page uses this implicitly.
In the statement, 'g(y)' was corrected by hand to 'g(x)'.

ideas.what: Identity theorem / analytic continuation for power series on intersecting polycylinders, proved by restriction to a segment and a sup argument
ideas.modern_name: Identity theorem (principle of analytic continuation) for several-variable analytic functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass); this formulation is Bourbaki-style, cf. Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats, and Dieudonné's Foundations of Modern Analysis
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook material (Bourbaki drafts, Dieudonné, Cartan's Théorie élémentaire des fonctions analytiques)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki-style draft page on the elementary identity theorem, reused as scratch paper. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics. Its only interest is archival: Grothendieck's motivic/Tannakian notes were written on the backs of Bourbaki drafts.
